title: Indexing & Slicing Tensors 🔪
description: Extract parts of a tensor using NumPy-style slicing and advanced indexing.

slides.title: Basic Indexing 🔢
slides.content:
# Like Python Lists, but Multi‑Axis

- Use square brackets `tensor[row, col, ...]`.
- Indices start at 0.
- Negative indices count from the end.

```python
t = tf.constant([[10,20,30],[40,50,60]])
t[0,1]   # 20
```

> Analogy: A bookshelf with shelves (axis 0) and positions on each shelf (axis 1).

slides.title: Multi‑Dimensional Indexing
slides.codeSnippet:
import tensorflow as tf

t3d = tf.constant([[[1,2],[3,4]], [[5,6],[7,8]]])
print(t3d[0,1,0])   # 3
print(t3d[1,0,1])   # 6

quizData.question: If `t = tf.constant([[1,2],[3,4],[5,6]])`, what is `t[-1,0]`?
quizData.explanation: Negative index -1 means last row (third row), column 0 gives value 5.

slides.title: Slicing Like a Pro 🍕
slides.content:
# The Colon `:` Syntax

- `start:stop:step` – works per axis.
- `:` alone means all elements along that axis.

```python
t = tf.constant([[10,20,30],[40,50,60],[70,80,90]])
t[1:, ::2]   # rows 1-end, columns skip by 2
# -> [[40,60],[70,90]]
```

slides.title: Practical Slicing
slides.codeSnippet:
t = tf.constant([[10,20,30],[40,50,60],[70,80,90]])
# first two rows, last two columns
sub = t[:2, 1:]
print(sub)   # [[20,30],[50,60]]

# every other element of first row
print(t[0,::2])  # [10,30]

slides.title: Advanced Indexing with `tf.gather` & `tf.gather_nd`
slides.content:
# Gather Slices by Index List

`tf.gather` picks out rows (or other axis) by index.
`tf.gather_nd` collects individual elements.

```python
params = tf.constant([[1,2],[3,4],[5,6]])
tf.gather(params, [0,2])   # rows 0 and 2 -> [[1,2],[5,6]]
tf.gather_nd(params, [[0,1],[2,0]])  # elements (0,1)=2, (2,0)=5
```
